findings.title: (2) resolveOwnerTier is a shared module function, NOT roster-scoped — but the admin page already computes an equivalent boolean for free
findings.detail:
`resolveOwnerTier(cfg, personId, fetchImpl?, dbEntityId?): Promise<'owner'|'editor'|'none'|'error'>` lives in `src/lib/nav/adminStore.ts:137-152`, alongside `resolveAdmin` and a shared `readDbRightsLists` helper (same file, lines 32-84) that both build on. It is a general module import, not tucked inside the roster route — importable and callable from the admin page exactly as the roster page calls it (`src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:349`), with the same `EntuCfg`-shaped `cfg` and the admin page's already-resolved `dbEntityId` (4th param) to skip a redundant resolve.

Today's ONLY caller is `src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:28,349` — the admin page (`src/routes/admin/+page.svelte`) imports `resolveAdmin` (line 34) but never `resolveOwnerTier`.

What the admin page already knows: it computes `canManageAdmins` (`+page.svelte:79`, set at line 180 from `listAdmins(...).canManage`). `listAdmins` (`src/lib/admin/roleManagement.ts:310-322`) reads the SAME entity/props (`entity/{dbEntityId}?props=_owner,_editor`, via `fetchRights`) and sets `canManage: allOwners.some(v => v.reference === viewerId)` — i.e. "is the viewer in the db entity's aggregated `_owner` (own or inherited)", which is semantically the same question `resolveOwnerTier(...) === 'owner'` answers for the same entity/person. So the admin page could derive owner-tier from data it already fetches, with zero extra round-trip, INSTEAD of adding a fresh `resolveOwnerTier` call.

Caveat before reusing it that way: `canManageAdmins` is a plain boolean that collapses 'loading', 'error', and genuine 'not-owner' all into `false` — it cannot distinguish "not yet known" from "confirmed not owner", whereas `resolveOwnerTier` (and the roster page's own gating, `ownerTier !== 'loading'` at `+page.svelte:4291`) treats those as different states. Reusing `canManageAdmins` as-is would need that ambiguity accepted, or a fresh `resolveOwnerTier` call added if the build wants the roster's honest not-yet-resolved vs not-owner distinction.

findings.title: (3) Uninvited-persons list: listJoinStates is directly reusable, one GET per roster member (parallelized), admin page currently pays none of this cost
findings.detail:
`listJoinStates(cfg, personIds, fetchImpl?): Promise<Record<string, 'absent'|'invited'|'joined'>>` — `src/lib/profile/linkedIdentities.ts:107-121`. It discriminates on `entu_user` entry CONTENTS (never presence), exactly per Mihkel's #294 rule quoted in its doc comment: `'joined'` = an entry carries `uid`; `'invited'` = an entry carries only a masked `invite`; `'absent'` = neither — this `'absent'` state is exactly "uninvited" for #301's purposes (and per the PO ruling quoted in #301, withdrawn people land here too since withdrawal leaves no marker).

Mechanism: for each personId it calls `listLinkedIdentities(cfg, personId, fetchImpl)` (same file, lines 39-77) — one `GET entity/{personId}?props=entu_user` per person — fanned out via `Promise.all` (`linkedIdentities.ts:113-119`), and it FAILS LOUD: any single person's HTTP failure rejects the whole call (no silent partial result).

Reusability: yes, directly — filter the returned record for `state === 'absent'`, map those personIds to `roster[].name` (admin page already loads `roster: RosterRow[]` via `loadRoster`, `+page.svelte:70` field + call at line ~275) to build the select's option labels. No new query needed; `listLinkedIdentities` alone is the per-person primitive `listJoinStates` already wraps, so calling it directly instead would just reimplement the fan-out.

Fan-out cost on the admin page: today the admin page does NOT call `listJoinStates`/`listLinkedIdentities` at all (only the roster page does, at `+page.svelte:349` region via `listJoinStates(cfg, rows.map(r=>r.personId))`). Adding it to the admin page means N additional parallel GETs per load, where N = roster size — the same shape/cost the roster page already accepts for its own three-state badges, just newly incurred on `/admin` too (which today loads roster only to feed the admin/librarian picker selects, not per-member state).

findings.title: (4) mintSelfLinkInvite signature, caller requirements, and the 403 path's actual granularity
findings.detail:
`mintSelfLinkInvite(cfg: EntuCfg, personId: string, fetchImpl: typeof fetch = fetch): Promise<{inviteToken: string}>` — `src/lib/invite/inviteData.ts:489-535`. `EntuCfg = {db: string; token: string}` (`src/lib/seasons/entuSeasons.ts:11-16`), structurally identical to the admin page's own `Cfg` type — no adapter needed. `personId` is an arbitrary person id, not restricted to the caller's own; despite the "self-link" name and doc-comment framing (#193 origin), the function itself places no restriction — #294's live probe (cited in its doc comment, `inviteData.ts:481-487`) confirmed it mints onto ANOTHER person's entity when the caller holds db-entity `_owner`.

Sequence: sweeps stale invite placeholders first (`sweepStaleInvitePlaceholders`, same file lines 384-424 — a GET then sequential DELETEs, all-or-nothing), THEN POSTs the mint trigger to `entity/{personId}`.

Error cases — all surface as `SelfLinkMintError` (`phase: 'identity-read'|'stale-invite-cleanup'|'mint'`, `reason: 'http'|'contract'|'missing-self-editor'`), a DIFFERENT class from `createInvite`'s `InviteCreateError` (see item 1) — a caller reusing InviteSurface's existing `catch (e) { if (e instanceof InviteCreateError) ... }` branch would NOT catch this type today.

The 403 path (`inviteData.ts:518-525`): the mint POST's `mintRes.status === 403` branch unconditionally labels the error `reason: 'missing-self-editor'` with message text "...the person lacks self-_editor" — but per #294's own probe (quoted in the doc comment two paragraphs up, `inviteData.ts:483-487`) the OBSERVED 403 in the caller-not-owner case carries Entu's own text "User not in _owner property", a different cause (caller's own rights tier, not the target person's grant). The code does not distinguish these two 403 causes — both land on the same `reason: 'missing-self-editor'` value with the same fixed message text, which would misdescribe the owner-gate case if surfaced verbatim to an admin.

findings.title: (5) No spec asserts the submit button's rendered label today; all coverage is testid-based, no dedicated InviteSurface.svelte spec exists
findings.detail:
There is no component-level spec file for `InviteSurface.svelte` itself — confirmed by listing `src/lib/components/admin/` (no `.spec.*` sibling) and by grep: every reference to `InviteSurface` outside its own file is either the admin/invite route wrapper or a page-level integration spec.

Specs that touch the submit control — `src/routes/page.admin-database.spec.ts`, `page.admin-invite-alignment.spec.ts`, `page.admin-invite-session-expired.spec.ts`, `page.admin-invite.spec.ts`, `page.navshell-merge.spec.ts` — all locate it exclusively by `[data-testid="invite-admin-submit"]` and assert only on presence, `.disabled`, and click behavior (calls into `createInvite`, produces a link). None reads `.textContent` or does a `getByRole('button', {name: ...})` lookup on it. The three files that stub `admin_invite_submit`/`admin_invite_creating` as mock message functions (`page.admin-invite.spec.ts:28-29`, `page.admin-invite-alignment.spec.ts:69-70`, `page.admin.spec.ts:92-93`) do so only to satisfy the `m.*` import surface, not to assert rendered text.

Practical consequence: changing the submit label based on selection state cannot break any EXISTING assertion (there is nothing today pinning the label's text), but it also means there is no existing spec to extend by example — new label-state coverage ("submit says today's behaviour" vs "submit names the selected person") would be new tests, not edits to existing ones.

findings.title: (6) i18n: four locale files kept in lockstep at parallel key positions; interpolation is a supported, precedented pattern
findings.detail:
`messages/en.json`, `et.json`, `lv.json`, `uk.json` all exist and are kept structurally parallel — e.g. `admin_invite_title`/`admin_invite_submit` sit at the SAME line numbers (59/65) across all four files. Any new key (select label, per-behaviour submit labels, default option text) needs an entry in all four, matching this existing key-ordering convention.

Interpolated messages are an established pattern, not a new capability to introduce: `admin_invite_show_once: "...It expires on {date}."` (`en.json:71`) and `admin_invite_partial_failure: "...({personId})..."` (`en.json:74`) already use `{param}` placeholders, so a person-naming submit label (e.g. `admin_invite_submit_person: "Invite {name}"`) fits the existing convention directly.

Reusable existing string for the non-owner explanation: `roster_member_invite_owner_only: "Managing invites requires owner rights."` (`en.json:238`), rendered today at `src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:4301` behind `data-testid="roster-invite-owner-note"`. Paraglide messages are plain exported functions (not component-scoped), so `m.roster_member_invite_owner_only()` is callable verbatim from the admin page/InviteSurface despite its `roster_`-prefixed key name — #301's text explicitly calls for reusing this exact line, so the choice is between importing it as-is (name mismatch, zero duplication) or adding a parallel `admin_`-prefixed key with identical text across all four locale files (naming consistency, some duplication) — a judgment call the build will need to make, not something resolvable by reading code.

findings.title: Additional verified nuance: admin page's roster names are NOT the real-names overlay the roster page shows
findings.detail: The admin page loads roster via `loadRoster(c)` (`src/routes/admin/+page.svelte` import list line ~36, call in `load()` around line 275) — the BASE resolution only (profile/public names). The roster page instead calls `loadRosterWithRealNames` (`src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:349` region), which overlays each collective's real `admin_member_record` name on top when `roster_show_real_names` is on (`src/lib/roster/rosterData.ts:392-430`). So if #301's select is fed straight from the admin page's existing `roster` state, the person-name labels shown there could differ from the names an owner sees on the roster page for the same collective when real-names display is enabled — worth flagging to whoever builds it, since the issue's spec ("labelled with the person's display name") doesn't specify which name source to use.

findings.title: Issue #302 items 1-3 (item 4 filed separately) — full body captured
findings.detail: [unverified→verified this turn] `gh issue view 302 --json title,body,comments` (plain `gh issue view --comments` printed nothing, JSON form worked). Filed 2026-09-09 by Gama (*PO:Gama*), zero comments. Item 1: pencil (`roster-row-record-edit-{memberId}`) goes away, whole card becomes the editor activator; constraint stated explicitly: the editor renders inside the same row block, so a plain `<button>` wrapping the card is illegal (nested-interactive) — 'the collapsed card is the activator; an open card is a form, not a button.' Two survivors required: real keyboard-operable element (not `<div onclick>`), and #262's content-derived accessible name, now scaled to the whole card. Done-when includes 'opening still works on the admin's own row — the record editor has no self-row exclusion and must not acquire one.' Item 2: join-state badge (`roster-row-join-state-{memberId}`) moves directly under name/email; 'joined' becomes silent (no chip); not-invited and invited-awaiting keep distinct chips (explicitly NOT dropping the awaiting chip, contra a literal reading of 'joined chip not needed'). Badge stays contents-derived via `listJoinStates`, visible to every admin tier. Item 3: invite + deactivate control groups move inside the opened editor. Three survivors flagged as 'easy to lose': (1) self-row asymmetry — deactivate's `row.personId !== selected?.personId` guard must persist even though it now shares a container with the editor, which has no such guard; (2) owner gating (`_owner`-only) and pure state-routing (absent→kutsu, invited→reinvite/tühista, joined→nothing) unchanged; (3) generation guards in `handleMintInvite`/`handleDeactivateConfirm` (hardened across #287/#296/#297/#299) — relocate render site only, don't reimplement. `roster-invite-owner-note` stays page-level (Gama's explicit, reversible call). Watch-for: `page.roster-pending-collective-switch.spec.ts` (#287's regression proof) must keep passing unedited; an edit to it 'deserves its own scrutiny.'

findings.detail:
The whole row is one `

    `, i.e. the editor renders inside the same `
  • ` the pencil lives in, exactly as the issue states. After that: the join-state badge block (3847-3940, admin-only, gated on `joinStates[row.personId] !== undefined`) — badge span itself (3857-3866), then (if `ownerTier === 'owner'`) the invite/reinvite/withdraw button cluster (3867-3907) state-routed off `state` ('absent'→invite btn 3876-3885, 'invited'→reinvite+withdraw 3886-3905, 'joined'→nothing), then the invite-link/error/withdraw-error paragraphs (3908-3939). Then the admin section-picker block (3941-3990, unrelated to this issue). Then the deactivate block (3992-4081, admin-only AND `row.personId !== selected?.personId`): armed/disarmed two-step confirm toggle (4010-4043) plus refusal/failure alerts (4044-4080). Note: contrary to the issue text's summary ('badge renders after the section name'), the code shows the badge currently renders AFTER the pencil/editor block, not immediately after the section span — it is not literally adjacent to name/email/section today; item 2's move puts it there for the first time.

findings.title: recordEditorMemberId gate confirmed nested inside the same row block — the load-bearing constraint
findings.detail: Line 3721: `{#if recordEditorMemberId === row.memberId}` sits directly inside the pencil's wrapping `<div>` (3702-3845), itself inside the `<li>` for that row. This is genuinely single-row-scoped state (comment at 1445-1448 confirms the top-level `recordEditorMemberId` var deliberately makes 'only one editor open at a time' true by construction — opening a different row's editor makes THIS row's `{#if}` false on the next tick, closing it). So: today the pencil `<button>` and the editor form are SIBLINGS inside one `<div>`, never nested inside each other — meaning today's markup does NOT already violate nested-interactive; the violation only appears if the whole COLLAPSED CARD becomes a `<button>` while the editor still renders as its sibling within the same `<li>`, because then the button and the editor's `<input>`s become button-descendant siblings... actually the concrete risk the issue names is a naive 'wrap everything in a button' refactor — the current structure's separation (button and editor as adjacent siblings, not button-wraps-editor) is exactly what must be preserved/extended: the fix should keep the collapsed-state and open-state as mutually exclusive alternatives (button XOR form), never one wrapping the other.

findings.title: Collapsed card DOM shape is <li>; page already has TWO precedent idioms for 'whole element becomes activator, editor is a state-swap not a nested child'
findings.detail: (a) roster/+page.svelte's own arrange-mode row precedent (lines 4630-4799, main): a `role="button"` `<div data-testid="arrange-row-{id}">` with `tabindex={active ? 0 : -1}`, `aria-label` from contents, `onkeydown={(e) => handleHandleKeydown(node, e)}`, and an `onclick` guarded `if (event.detail !== 0) return;` (comment #152 review F1: 'honour the role=button activation promise arriving as a click, without letting a pointer gesture near the grab state machine') — extensively commented (4568-4838) on the exact nested-interactive (WCAG 4.1.2) trap: two buttons used to live INSIDE the role=button row and were hoisted OUT as siblings specifically because focusable controls inside a role=button row is the violation, and because the row's own accessible name (computed from contents) picked up the nested buttons' text. Rename mode there is a `{#if renamingSectionId === row.id}...{:else}...{/if}` SWAP between the reorder-row markup and a separate rename `<input>` row — never one nested inside the other. (b) admin/+page.svelte:562-589 (main) 'whole-field' idiom explicitly cross-referenced by roster's own comment at 4747-4748 ('#205 whole-field shape, see admin/+page.svelte:513-540 and the season panel above'): collapsed state is a real `<button data-testid="admin-collective-name-edit">` sized `min-h-11 w-full` (not a bare pencil) with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the value span and an sr-only action-label child; editing state is a completely separate `<input>` swapped in via `{#if editingName}...{:else}...{/if}` — button and input never coexist as parent/child. This {#if}/{:else} swap between 'activator element' and 'form element,' already used twice on this page's ecosystem, is the reusable shape for the card. Keyboard machinery worth reusing directly: `handleHandleKeydown`'s Enter/Space `preventDefault()` + activate pattern (roster/+page.svelte:3417-3421) and the roving-tabindex helpers (`moveFocus`, `handleElementFor`, lines ~3255-3320) if the card needs to participate in a keyboard-navigable list; simpler card-only activation likely just needs a real `<button>`/`role="button"`+tabindex+onkeydown Enter/Space, no roving tabindex required since cards aren't currently a single composite widget.

Implementation: `{m.roster_record_edit_label()} {row.profileName ?? row.name}` nested inside the `

findings.title: Specs asserting on the pencil, badge, or driving the editor open — complete enumeration
findings.detail:
Repo-wide grep (`grep -rl "roster-row-record-edit\|roster-row-join-state"`) across src (no e2e dir in repo) returns exactly three spec files plus the page itself — nothing else in the tree touches either testid.

1. `src/routes/page.roster-record-editor.spec.ts` — the primary contract file, ~90 call sites. Shared helper `openEditor(container, memberId)` (lines 236-242): `fireEvent.click(q(container, 'roster-row-record-edit-' + memberId))` then `waitFor` on `roster-record-name` appearing inside that row's `<li>`. Used at ~85 call sites throughout describe blocks (B) through (F) (saves, prefill, damaged-data guard interplay, generation guards, collective-switch discard, i18n). Fixing this ONE function's click target is what the issue means by 'update the helpers, not weaken assertions.' TWO call sites bypass the helper with inline clicks on the raw testid: line 449 (damaged-data test, inlined because the helper's waitFor on `roster-record-name` would never resolve when the lookup is damaged) and — separately — describe block (A) 'pencil affordance' (lines 257-310, 6 tests) makes DIRECT existence/absence/content assertions on `roster-row-record-edit-{id}` with no editor ever opened: presence on another's row (260), presence on admin's OWN row / no self-exclusion (263-266), absence for non-admin (268-271), the #262 content-derived-name check (273-280, quoted above), presence in flat-list view (282-287), presence in an expanded section group (289-302), and absence in arrange mode (304-309). Every one of these breaks outright when the pencil element is deleted — they assert the pencil's EXISTENCE, not just use it as a means to open the form, so they must be rewritten to assert on the new whole-card activator's testid, not merely re-pointed.

2. `src/routes/page.roster-real-names.spec.ts` — two direct (non-helper) hits: line 395, an existence assertion `expect(q(container, 'roster-row-record-edit-m2')).not.toBeNull()` used as a #268/#269 baseline fence ('the record-editor pencil belongs to both sides' of the real-names toggle) — breaks outright; line 474, a direct `fireEvent.click(q(container, 'roster-row-record-edit-m2'))` to drive the editor open for a create-path-prefill assertion (checks the prefill uses `profileName` not the displayed real name) — this is a second, unshared 'drive the editor open' code path outside the shared `openEditor` helper and must be updated independently of it.

3. `src/routes/page.roster-join-state.spec.ts` — badge-value assertions, all via the shared `q()`/`waitFor` idiom (no separate helper). Lines 279-287: asserts an owner-admin sees 'one badge per row' including `roster-row-join-state-m2` present with `data-join-state="joined"` — this is the test most directly falsified by item 2 ('joined member shows no badge'): the element won't exist at all under the new contract, so this test fails outright, not just its value-check. Line 301-307 (editor-admin sees the same three badges, waits on m2/joined again) fails the same way. Lines 289-299 (invited-never-joined trap, m3) and 306-307/426/479/499/565-600 (m3/m4/m-bob invited/absent assertions) are UNAFFECTED in shape (those states keep their chip) but several are gated behind a `waitFor(() => expect(q(container,'roster-row-join-state-m2')).not.toBeNull())` (lines 281-283, 303-304) used purely as a 'roster has loaded' readiness gate before asserting on m3/m4 — those waits must be repointed at a state that still renders (or at a different readiness signal) since m2 (joined) will no longer produce an element to wait on. Line 312 (non-admin sees zero badges, `querySelectorAll` length 0) is unaffected. No DOM-order/adjacency assertion between the badge and name/email/section exists anywhere in this file or the others searched — the 'moves directly under name/email' requirement is currently unpinned by any spec, so item 2's reposition has no existing regression guard to satisfy or break, only new coverage to add.

No other spec file in the repo (verified by the same grep, zero additional hits) references either testid, including `page.roster-pending-collective-switch.spec.ts` (the #287 regression proof the issue explicitly calls out as must-stay-green) and `page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts` — neither touches the pencil or badge testids, consistent with the issue's framing that they're a different concern.

findings.title: Self-row asymmetry — deactivate gate quoted, record editor confirmed to carry no equivalent exclusion
findings.detail: Deactivate block gate, src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:3992: `{#if admin === 'admin' && row.personId !== selected?.personId}` — the entire deactivate control cluster (armed/disarmed buttons, refusal alert, failure alert, lines 3992-4081) is absent from the DOM whenever the row belongs to the currently-selected admin (`selected?.personId`), by construction of the render condition itself (the comment at 3993-3995 states this is #255's done-when 7: 'a member cannot deactivate herself... via a control she can't even see for her own row'). The record-editor's own gate, by contrast, at line 3696 is bare `{#if admin === 'admin'}` — no `row.personId !== selected?.personId` term at all — and the comment directly above the pencil button (3697-3701) makes the contrast explicit and deliberate: 'the contract has NO self-row exclusion (unlike the deactivate block below, which never lets an admin act on her own row)... deliberately not copy-pasting the `row.personId !== selected?.personId` guard.' `page.roster-record-editor.spec.ts:263-266` pins this with a named test: "the pencil IS present on the admin's OWN row — the contract has no self-row exclusion (deactivate-guard copy-paste trap)". Consequence for item 3 (moving deactivate INTO the editor, which itself has no self-exclusion): the merge point must keep applying the `row.personId !== selected?.personId` test to the deactivate sub-block specifically, even once it's a child of the self-exclusion-free editor container — the issue's own item-3 point 1 states this outcome directly ('the two guards do not merge just because the controls now share a container').

findings.title: 1. Invite controls (kutsu / saada uuesti / tühista kutse) — current render block

All three live inside the `memberRow` snippet (src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:3681), in the sibling `{#if admin === 'admin' && joinStates[row.personId] !== undefined}` block at lines 3847-3940. The three buttons themselves sit in a nested owner-only gate:

The outer gate is `admin === 'admin' && joinStates[row.personId] !== undefined` — routing is 'PURELY off `state`' per the inline comment at 3868-3874.

findings.title: 2. Deactivate armed-pair block — current render location
findings.detail:
Also a sibling block inside `memberRow`, at lines 3992-4081: `{#if admin === 'admin' && row.personId !== selected?.personId}` (never on the viewer's own row, per the #255 comment at 3992-4009).

Inside, arm-state routing at 4011 `{#if pendingDeactivateId === row.memberId}`:
  - armed branch: confirm button testid `member-deactivate-confirm-{row.memberId}` (4013-4022), `disabled={deactivatePending}` `aria-busy={deactivatePending}`, `onclick={() => handleDeactivateConfirm(row)}`; cancel button testid `member-deactivate-cancel-{row.memberId}` (4023-4031), `disabled={deactivatePending}`, `onclick={() => disarmDeactivate(row.memberId)}`.
  - else branch: trigger button testid `member-deactivate-{row.memberId}` (4033-4041), `disabled={deactivatePending}`, `onclick={() => armDeactivate(row.memberId)}`.

Followed by two more alerts gated on `pendingDeactivateId === row.memberId` plus their own error slot: refusal `member-deactivate-refused-{row.memberId}` (4044-4064) and action-error `member-deactivate-failed-{row.memberId}` (4065-4080).

findings.title: 3. `row` binding is unaffected by relocating inside the record editor's block
findings.detail: All of the above blocks are siblings, at the same nesting depth, within ONE `{#snippet memberRow(row: RosterRow, showSection: boolean)}` (3681). The record editor's own gate is `{#if recordEditorMemberId === row.memberId}` at line 3721, nested one level inside `{#if admin === 'admin'}` (3696). Because `row` is the snippet's own parameter — not something re-bound by any ancestor `{#if}` — it is identically in scope whether a block sits as a direct child of the `<li>` or nested inside the 3721 conditional. Moving the invite/deactivate/owner-note-adjacent blocks inside 3721 changes only DOM nesting depth, not what `row` refers to: `row.memberId`, `row.personId`, `handleMintInvite(row)`, `armDeactivate(row.memberId)`, etc. all resolve to the exact same object. Likewise none of the closed-over reactive state (`joinStates`, `ownerTier`, `inviteActionPending`, `inviteLinkByMemberId`, `inviteErrorByMemberId`, `withdrawErrorByMemberId`, `pendingDeactivateId`, `deactivatePending`, `deactivateRefusal`, `deactivateActionError`, `admin`, `selected`) is itself parented to a particular render location — they're plain `$state`/`$derived`/module-level reads, read directly wherever the markup that references them happens to sit. So no binding changes from the relocation itself; the outer gates on each block (`row.personId !== selected?.personId` for deactivate, `joinStates[row.personId] !== undefined` for invite) still need to be preserved verbatim as nested conditions inside the new location, since the record editor's own gate (`admin === 'admin'` alone, deliberately with NO self-row exclusion per the 3697-3701 comment) is weaker than deactivate's.

findings.title: 4. Owner note `roster-invite-owner-note` — stays page-level, confirmed
findings.detail: Rendered once at lines 4291-4302, `{#if admin === 'admin' && ownerTier !== 'owner' && ownerTier !== 'loading'}`, OUTSIDE the `memberRow` snippet entirely — it sits in the main results block (`{:else}` branch starting 4290), a sibling of the section-load-error/reorder-error/remove-error banners, not per-row. The comment at 4295-4299 explicitly says it's rendered ONCE for the whole page rather than per row. This matches the issue's instruction that it stays page-level.

findings.title: 5. Specs driving these controls at their CURRENT (pre-relocation) location — all need a two-click (open-editor-first) update
findings.detail:
grep across src/**/*.spec.ts for the six testid prefixes turns up exactly four files, and NONE of them open the record editor first (`grep -n 'record-edit|recordEditor'` returns zero hits in three of the four, and only an unrelated comment in the fourth):

- src/routes/page.roster-join-state.spec.ts — direct queries/clicks on `roster-member-invite-{id}` / `roster-member-reinvite-{id}` / `roster-member-withdraw-{id}` / `roster-invite-link-{id}` / `roster-invite-error-{id}` / `roster-withdraw-error-{id}` / `roster-invite-owner-note` throughout (lines 243, 329-667 per grep — e.g. 401 `fireEvent.click(q(container,'roster-member-invite-m4'))`, 653-654 also clicks `member-deactivate-m2`/`member-deactivate-confirm-m2` directly). Every one of these drive-paths needs the editor opened first if the controls move inside it.
- src/routes/page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts — the #286 armed-pair lifecycle spec named in the issue. Every click/assert on `member-deactivate-*` (dozens of sites, e.g. 179-1191 per grep) goes directly against the row-level control; zero editor-open calls anywhere in the file (only a comment at line 729 mentioning 'record-editor... cancel' unrelated to opening it).
- src/routes/page.roster-pending-collective-switch.spec.ts — see finding 6.
- src/routes/page.roster-stale-flags-collective-switch.spec.ts — NOT named in the issue but also directly drives `member-deactivate-{memberId}`/`member-deactivate-confirm-{memberId}` via its own helper (lines 378-382) and asserts `member-deactivate-failed-m-bob` / `member-deactivate-refused-m-bob` / `member-deactivate-confirm-m-bob` (lines 777-845) with no editor-open step. This file is entangled by the same relocation and is outside the issue's named scope — flagging it since it will break the same way as roster-deactivate.spec.ts if not updated.

No spec file references the invite/deactivate testids AND opens the editor first — so 'update the drive path to two-click' is not optional cleanup, it is required for every one of these four files once the markup moves.

findings.title: 6. `page.roster-pending-collective-switch.spec.ts` CANNOT pass unchanged — the issue's own constraint is unsatisfiable as literally stated
findings.detail:
The issue requires this spec to pass UNCHANGED. Verified it directly exercises the deactivate controls at their current row-level location via a private helper `startHeldDeactivate` (scratchpad copy lines ~311-321): `fireEvent.click(q(container, 'member-deactivate-{memberId}'))` then waits for `member-deactivate-confirm-{memberId}` then clicks it — invoked from both tests in the `#287 deactivatePending across a collective switch` describe block (STALE DISABLE, ~line 451-470; LATE-SETTLE CLOBBER, ~line 473-527), including direct `.disabled`/`aria-busy` assertions on `member-deactivate-m-bob` / `member-deactivate-confirm-m-bob` / `member-deactivate-cancel-m-bob`. There is no code path in this file that opens the record editor before touching these testids. If the deactivate block's render site moves inside `{#if recordEditorMemberId === row.memberId}` (i.e. behind the two-click open-editor-first flow), `q(container, 'member-deactivate-m-ada')` returns null at the very first `startHeldDeactivate` call and the helper throws (fireEvent.click on null) or the subsequent `waitFor` times out — the spec fails outright, it does not merely need a cosmetic touch-up.

This is the loud flag the issue itself asks for: 'unchanged' is not actually achievable for this file under a pure markup relocation — the drive path (both `startHeldDeactivate` call sites, i.e. every call to that helper in the file) requires an edit to open the row's record editor before arming deactivate, exactly like the #286 spec in finding 5. That edit is itself a change to a file the issue explicitly wants untouched, and per the issue's own instruction it 'gets its own scrutiny' before being made.

findings.title: 5b/6b. #286 lifecycle spec (`page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts`) — same unchanged-ness question, same answer
findings.detail: Same finding as above, restated for the file the issue names directly under item 6: every click in page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts against `member-deactivate-{memberId}` / `member-deactivate-confirm-{memberId}` / `member-deactivate-cancel-{memberId}` (grep shows dozens of call sites spanning lines 179-1191) targets the row-level control directly, with zero prior editor-open step anywhere in the file. If this spec is meant to keep passing after the relocation, its drive path needs the same 'open editor first' edit as page.roster-join-state.spec.ts and page.roster-pending-collective-switch.spec.ts — it is not exempt just because it's the file that originally pinned the #286 armed-pair lifecycle. The issue frames #286/#287 lifecycle behavior as off-limits to re-derive, but the RENDER-LOCATION move still forces a drive-path (not logic) edit here, which is a distinct thing from re-deriving the generation guards, and should be called out as such rather than silently bundled into 'just move the markup.'
